title: Adaptive Prospectivity Ladder: Model-Fit Experiments & Scouting Framework
creator: Ava Chen
summary: Define and run a small-batch experimental program that creates an "adaptable prospectivity ladder" — a ranked, evidence-backed scoring system that evaluates candidate open models for target enterprise segments (latency-sensitive RAG, embeddings-heavy search, regulated PII workflows). The ladder produces procurement signals and a short list of ready-to-deploy variants with recommended quantization/hardware pairings.
goals: Produce a 20-item scoring rubric mapping model attributes to enterprise fit (latency threshold, accuracy on domain prompts, quantization friendliness, cost-per-1000-token estimate)
Run 6 quickbench probes across representative prospect workloads and synthesize results into a prospectivity score per model-flavor
Ship a minimal dashboard + CSV export for SRE/Platform to consume signals and trigger Dedicated/Private onboarding experiments
acceptance_criteria: Scoring rubric documented in Confluence with definitions for every metric and weighting rationale
Bench results for at least 8 model variants (open and vendor-available) uploaded to shared Drive and mapped to rubric scores
Dashboard prototype accessible to product, eng, and solutions teams with filters for vertical, latency bucket, and token-cost
Clear procurement triggers (e.g., score >= 0.78 & latency < 120ms regionally) documented for sales/ops handoff
deliverables: Confluence doc: Adaptive Prospectivity Ladder (definitions + methodology)
Bench workbook (Drive): raw runs, cost calc sheet, normalization steps
Handoff note for Solutions & Sales with priority candidate list and suggested SLA tiers
approach_summary: We will use an evidence-first experiment loop: (1) create vertical-specific prompt suites (RAG, embeddings, NLU) representative of enterprise prospects; (2) run short microbench jobs across candidate models focusing on latency distributions, token-level cost, and regression on key prompt sets; (3) normalize results and compute a composite prospectivity score; (4) surface top candidates and quick recommendations for quantization and hardware pairing. Emphasis is on relative comparators rather than absolute claims.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Model behavior variance across prompt sets can skew scores. Mitigation: use stratified prompt sampling and bootstrap confidence intervals.
Risk: Bench environment mismatch with customer infra. Mitigation: annotate results with hardware affinity and run at least one sample on Dedicated-like instance types.
Risk: Procurement triggers might be gamed by vendors optimizing to the benchmark. Mitigation: maintain a rotating prompt set and include adversarial holdouts in the eval suite.
milestones: 2025-02-18: finalize rubric and vertical prompt suites
2025-02-25: complete first wave bench runs (4 models)
2025-03-02: integrate normalization, compute prospectivity scores, and seed dashboard
2025-03-18: run second wave (expanded model set + region-specific latency checks)
2025-03-28: handoff short-list to Solutions & Sales; create procurement triggers

notes: Prefer lightweight, repeatable microbench jobs rather than long, single-run experiments so we can iterate weekly.
Coordinate with PMs owning target vertical playbooks (finserv, legal, search) to get representative prompt suites.
Keep the rubric transparent: include per-metric rationale so sales and procurement understand tradeoffs.
outcomes: Outcome A: A ranked short-list of 6 model variants with prospectivity scores and recommended deployment tier (Hosted/Dedicated/Private)
Outcome B: A calibrated procurement trigger set that Sales can use to recommend reserved capacity or pilot offers
Outcome C: A reproducible bench kit for future model additions and a lightweight dashboard for continuous monitoring
